source: Cemri et al. (2025) Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST)
finding: Berkeley team built a taxonomy of 14 failure modes in 3 categories from multi-agent LLM traces. Failure rates of the 7 systems were 41% to 86.7%.
numbers: 1,642 annotated traces, 7 frameworks (MetaGPT, ChatDev, HyperAgent, AppWorld, AG2, Magentic-One, OpenManus). Taxonomy built on 150+ traces by 6 experts. Human kappa 0.88.
limits: Not claimed exhaustive. Closed systems excluded for lack of traces. Text says 7 systems, one figure caption says 6.
agent_relevance: Gives the closest LLM analogue of Woods's failure patterns. A map of what to monitor for.

source: Cemri et al. (2025) Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST)
finding: System design failures were the largest group. Step repetition (stuck in the same behaviour) and unaware of termination were the biggest single modes.
numbers: FC1 system design 44.2% total (my sum): step repetition 15.7%, unaware of termination 12.4%, disobey task spec 11.8%, loss of history 2.8%, disobey role 1.5%.
limits: Percentages are per trace, one trace can have several modes.
agent_relevance: Stuck-in-outdated-behaviour maps to step repetition. Needs a code-side repetition counter, not model self-report.

source: Cemri et al. (2025) Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST)
finding: Inter-agent misalignment (working at cross purposes) was the second group. Biggest modes were reasoning-action mismatch and task derailment.
numbers: FC2 32.4% total (my sum): reasoning-action mismatch 13.2%, task derailment 7.4%, fail to ask clarification 6.8%, conversation reset 2.2%, ignored other agent 1.9%, information withholding 0.85%.
limits: One agent here, so FC2 applies only if the scaffold uses several model calls with roles.
agent_relevance: Reasoning-action mismatch is also an issue for a single agent: stated plan not matching tool call. Check in code.

source: Cemri et al. (2025) Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST)
finding: Verification failures were 23.5% of the modes. Incorrect verification was more common than no verification.
numbers: FC3 (my sum): incorrect verification 9.1%, no or incomplete verification 8.2%, premature termination 6.2%.
limits: Same caveats as above.
agent_relevance: Supports guardrail G3 and G2: a verifier that is itself wrong is a main failure source.

source: Cemri et al. (2025) Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST)
finding: Simple prompt and workflow fixes helped only a little. Adding a high-level objective verification step helped most.
numbers: ChatDev: role spec plus workflow change (CEO has final say) +9.4% task success with GPT-4o. Added verification step up to +15.6% on ProgramDev.
limits: Gains inconsistent across case studies. ProgramDev chosen to be easy. Task completion stayed low.
agent_relevance: Prompt-level patches do not fix structural failure. Matches schema stance that code, not prompts, must carry control.

source: Cemri et al. (2025) Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST)
finding: An LLM annotator (o1) can label failure modes in traces at fair agreement. Few-shot clearly beat zero-shot.
numbers: Few-shot: accuracy 0.94, kappa 0.77, F1 0.80. Zero-shot: accuracy 0.89, kappa 0.58. Out-of-domain kappa 0.79.
limits: Some failure modes correlate up to 0.63, so symptoms may be conflated.
agent_relevance: A monitor model can tag impasse patterns, but a code check is cheaper and G5 says code selects.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) MIRAGE-Bench: LLM Agent is Hallucinating and Where to Find Them
finding: Benchmark of agent behaviour in risky snapshots. One scenario tests loops: the agent already repeated a failed action 3 or 6 times; does it change course and show it noticed?
numbers: Flawed-interaction-history-repetitive: GPT-4o utility 0.572, hallucination rate 0.345. Claude-3.7-Sonnet 0.624 / 0.325. Qwen2.5-7B 0.595 / 0.351. Overall utility typically below 0.6 for all models.
quote: repeating the same action three times already exceeds typical bounds of human trial-and-error
limits: Snapshots from WebArena with GPT-4o-mini and Qwen2.5-72B traces. LLM judge, temperature 0. Judge accuracy above 0.75 vs other judges. DeepSeek runs incomplete.
agent_relevance: Direct measure of stuck-in-outdated-behaviour. Scale does not remove it, so a code-side impasse detector is justified.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) MIRAGE-Bench
finding: Authors note that humans adjust after a few failed attempts, but agents keep issuing invalid actions (example: clicking a button id that does not exist, with reasoning that flips each step).
numbers: Repetition snapshots are taken at the 3rd and 6th repeat. Strong models and 7B models score alike on this category (0.57-0.63 utility).
limits: Descriptive qualitative cases plus judge scores.
agent_relevance: Use a code rule: same action and same failing output twice triggers a reframe (G1 signal).

source: Liu and Meng (2026) Self-Correction as Feedback Control
finding: Treats self-correction as a two-state error chain. Iterate only if correction rate / introduction rate exceeds Acc/(1-Acc). Verify-first prompt removes harm.
numbers: 7 models, GSM8K, MATH, StrategyQA. o3-mini +3.4 pp, Claude Opus 4.6 +0.6 pp, o4-mini 0, GPT-5 and 4 others lost accuracy. GPT-4o-mini verify-first: error introduction 2% to 0%, -6.2 pp to +0.2 pp (McNemar p<1e-4).
limits: Abstract page only read, not the full paper. Gains need better correction rate, said to need training.
agent_relevance: Learn/respond function: revising from an unverified opinion can reduce accuracy. Supports G2.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without outside feedback, self-correction did not help and often lowered accuracy. With oracle labels it helped.
numbers: GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 (round 1) to 89.0 (round 2). GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1. Llama-2 GSM8K 62.0 to 43.5 to 36.5. Oracle: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3, GPT-4 HotpotQA 49 to 59.
limits: GPT-4 HotpotQA flat at round 1, so not every cell fell. 2023-era models; Liu and Meng 2026 show some newer ones no longer degrade.
agent_relevance: The feedback has to come from real output. Looking back without a signal is harmful.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Multi-agent debate did not beat plain self-consistency at equal numbers of responses.
numbers: GSM8K: standard 76.7. Self-consistency 3 responses 82.5, 6: 85.3, 9: 88.2. Debate 6 responses 83.2, 9 responses 83.0.
limits: One dataset, GPT-3.5.
agent_relevance: Supports G4: more voices from one model is not independence; vote in code.

source: Laban et al. (2025) LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation
finding: Models drop sharply when the task is given over several turns. Most of the drop is unreliability, not lost ability.
numbers: Average drop 39% across 6 generation tasks, 200,000+ simulated conversations. Small aptitude loss, large unreliability increase.
quote: when LLMs take a wrong turn in a conversation, they get lost and do not recover
limits: Abstract only read; model list and mitigations not seen.
agent_relevance: Close to Woods's decompensation: early wrong assumption locks in and the system does not recover. Restart from a clean restatement.

source: Cognitive Companion (2026) parallel monitor for looping and drift in LLM agents
finding: A silent observer watches the agent and whispers guidance when it loops. LLM monitor cut repetition on the Liar Paradox task; the average effect across tasks was zero.
numbers: Gemma 4 E4B. E1 Liar Paradox: Jaccard repetition 0.367 to 0.176 (-52%). LLM monitor overhead about 11%. E2 aggregate LLM monitor +0.014 +/- 0.723, i.e. no reduction; baseline won 3 of 6 tasks.
limits: Feasibility study, tiny runs (3 runs per condition, 6 steps), no significance tests, self-judged quality, lexical Jaccard only.
agent_relevance: The monitor idea is the Monitor potential. But a model monitor was not reliably better than nothing.

source: Cognitive Companion (2026)
finding: A hidden-state probe monitor had zero overhead and larger effect sizes, but was trained on tiny proxy-labelled data.
numbers: Probe mean Cohen d +0.471 +/- 0.893 vs LLM monitor +0.047 +/- 0.658. Layer 28 CV AUROC 0.84 on 35 examples (10 degraded). Second session: 32 examples, 3 degraded, AUROC undefined.
limits: Labels came from the LLM monitor's own output. Table 9 category means disagree with Table 5.
agent_relevance: Treat as a pointer only. Not usable inside an API-only scaffold.

source: Cognitive Companion (2026)
finding: Monitor did not help small models and could hurt structured tasks.
numbers: Qwen 2.5 1.5B and Llama 3.2 1B: quality change 0.000, 0 of 3 tasks improved each. Structured tasks LLM monitor d about -0.29 in one table.
limits: Possible scale boundary. Quality proxy is simple.
agent_relevance: Doubt only on a signal (G1): monitoring on structured tasks adds noise.

source: Circular Reasoning: Understanding Self-Reinforcing Loops (2026) LoopBench
finding: Reasoning models fall into numeric and statement loops. Loop rates are high on LoopBench and low on normal benchmarks.
numbers: LoopBench 700 items, 7 subtasks. Worst: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B 62.0% combined (17.14% numeric, 44.86% statement). Best API model gemini-2.5-pro 7.43%. AIME25 max 10.0%, SuperGPQA max 7.5%. At T=0.1 the 7B model reached 92.07%.
limits: Mostly DeepSeek and Qwen families. Arithmetic and recursive tasks only. Text and Table 1 disagree on proprietary rates.
agent_relevance: Loops get worse at low temperature. A restart with different sampling is a cheap response.

source: Circular Reasoning (2026) LoopBench
finding: Loop onset can be detected early from hidden states with a change-point test, with persistence needed to control false alarms.
numbers: CUSUM on a linear probe score: early detection rate 0.64-0.76, false positive 0.24-0.34, lead 36-52 sentences (about 1,300-1,900 tokens). Without persistence, false positives 0.40-0.62.
limits: Needs open weights. Calibrated on 50 non-loop cases per model.
agent_relevance: The persistence rule (several consecutive steps) is portable to text-level repetition checks in code.

source: Or (2025) MTTR-A: Measuring Cognitive Recovery Latency in Multi-Agent Systems
finding: Adapts mean-time-to-recovery to agent reasoning drift, split into detect, decide, execute. Tested four recovery reflexes in a LangGraph workflow.
numbers: 200 runs. Median recovery 6.21 s +/- 2.14 (P90 10.73 s). Normalised recovery ratio 0.077. Per reflex median: tool-retry 4.46 s, auto-replan 5.94, rollback 6.99, human-approve 12.22. Execution dominates the cost.
limits: Semi-simulated: synthetic drift on AG News, controlled reflex latencies. Measures time, not whether the answer got better.
agent_relevance: Gives a metric for the Respond potential. Rollback and replan are cheap; human gating is about 2x slower.

source: Xiao, Sun, Chen (2026) AIR: Improving Agent Safety through Incident Response
finding: Puts detect-contain-recover-eradicate (learn) inside the agent loop as a rule language. Rules written after an incident block similar ones later.
numbers: Three agent types (code, embodied, computer-use). Abstract: detection, remediation, eradication success all above 90%. False positives: 0 of 50 safe embodied tasks and 0 of 35 safe browser tasks.
limits: Authors' own benchmarks; code agent remediation not scored because effects are irreversible. Per-case rates vary (some 84-89%).
agent_relevance: Closest working use of respond plus learn in a loop. Learned rules are generated and applied by code, as G5 wants.

source: Xiao, Sun, Chen (2026) AIR
finding: Ablation: letting the agent invent its own remediation was worse and slower than a rule-specified one.
numbers: Embodied: remediation success 80.95% self vs 92.31% AIR, response 28.7 s vs 22.2 s. Computer-use: 76.60% vs 97.73%, 34.6 s vs 25.9 s.
limits: Small task sets. Rules author is also an LLM-assisted pipeline.
agent_relevance: After a failure the model must rebuild the causal chain, which is hard. Give it the located failing output (G2).

source: Liu et al. (2026) Resilience Matters for Embodied Agents System
finding: Builds metrics from resilience engineering (rebound, stability, graceful extensibility) and applies them to 10 embodied LLM systems on 400 household tasks. Systems with the same success rate differ a lot in recovery.
numbers: Reflexion 56.3% SR vs CoPAL 55.8% SR, but Reflexion recovery cost 4.8x higher (57.3 vs 11.9). ReAct SR 38.5% with lowest recovery cost 6.5. AgentEvolver stress capacity 0.21, CoPAL 0.85.
limits: Simulated household tasks; Hollnagel Safety-I and Safety-II are cited. Metrics defined by the authors.
agent_relevance: Outcome score hides resilience. Track steps wasted after a failure, not only final success.

source: Liu et al. (2026) Resilience Matters for Embodied Agents System
finding: Targeted repairs guided by the metrics improved the targeted trait but cost another one.
numbers: Rebound fix: recovery cost 59.11 to 33.73 (-42.9%). Stability fix: 51.01 to 43.01 recovery cost. Graceful extensibility fix: stress capacity improved but recovery cost 36.70 to 99.59 (+171%).
limits: Single benchmark; tradeoff stated by authors.
agent_relevance: Resilience is a trade-off, so do not add every potential. Pay for each at equal tokens (G7).

source: Cooperative Resilience in AI Multiagent Systems (2024)
finding: Defines resilience as anticipate, prepare, resist, recover, transform and measures it in a commons-harvest game with GPT-4 generative agents vs PPO agents.
numbers: Melting Pot 2.0 Commons Harvest Open. 9 apple-removal scenarios plus bot-intrusion runs. Averaged over 5 episodes. LLM agents scored above RL in all 3 bot experiments; LLM agents changed behaviour after bots left, RL did not.
limits: Preliminary. Numbers only in heatmaps. One environment. Some non-monotone results unexplained.
agent_relevance: Shows LLM agents adapt after a disruption; resilience scored from a reference curve, which code can compute.

source: Systems-theoretic analysis of loss of control (2026) STECA, STPA, FRAM on a coding-agent scenario
finding: Applies FRAM to a frontier-lab coding agent. Found four resonance patterns where normal variability, not a broken part, creates risk.
numbers: 6 functions modelled. 4 patterns: correlated control drift, model swap discontinuity, codebase saturation, rationale-anchored review. STECA about 50 completeness items over a 21-row control structure; 8 hazards in STPA.
limits: Built from public documents, not observed work. LLMs helped the analysis. No severity ranking.
agent_relevance: Rationale-anchored review is the same as grading by the model's own explanation. Check the output, not the stated intent (G2, G5).

source: Self-Healing Framework for Reliable LLM-Based Autonomous Agents (2026)
finding: Loop of detect, score reliability, heal by replan, prompt correction or tool re-selection. Four failure types: hallucination, execution error, reasoning inconsistency, workflow propagation.
numbers: GPT-5 base, faults injected at 30% probability, baselines: none, simple retry, Self-Refine. No numbers reported in the page read.
limits: Only qualitative claims, preliminary, weights and threshold unspecified.
agent_relevance: Fault-type to repair mapping is a usable lookup table in code.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Where LLM Agents Fail and How They Can Learn From Failures (AgentDebug)
finding: Finds the root-cause step in failed agent runs and feeds back corrective notes. Errors cascade from one early mistake.
numbers: 17% higher step accuracy and 24% higher all-correct accuracy than strongest baseline; up to 26% relative task-success gain on ALFWorld, GAIA, WebShop.
limits: Abstract only read.
agent_relevance: Locating the first bad step is the useful part of Look back.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion
finding: Agents write a verbal lesson after failure and retry. This is a learn loop inside the agent.
numbers: HumanEval pass@1 91% vs 80% for GPT-4 baseline.
limits: Abstract only read. Huang et al. show gains depend on an external signal.
agent_relevance: Reflexion-style memory works when the failure signal is real (test result), not self-judged.

source: Search results for practitioner pages on agent resilience (AWS blog, vendor posts) 2025-2026
finding: A search found no arXiv paper applying Woods's graceful extensibility or Safety-II to LLM agent evaluation except 2608.23839 and 2606.13474. Rest are practitioner posts (fault injection, graceful degradation, human handoff).
numbers: No measured results in the snippets.
limits: Search snippets only, not opened.
agent_relevance: Gap in the literature: no study yet tests the four potentials as a scaffold.
